findings.title: Garden speech is selectively ordered
findings.claim: The focus's auditory rule participates in a wider Garden pattern in which futile speech is removed and peace remains as positive utterance, so the exception gives the quiet place a defined speech environment rather than an empty silence.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are يَسْمَعُونَ, لَغْوًا, and سَلَامًا. The supplied target Arabic and connection notes at 78:35, 56:25, 88:11, and 52:23 repeatedly pair Garden hearing with the exclusion of laghw, while 56:26, 10:10, 13:24, and 36:58 supply peace as admitted or received speech. These wider contacts return through the focus hearing, futile-speech, and peace words and change the scene into a selectively ordered soundscape.
findings.reader_payoff: The place is perceived as quiet through the removal of a kind of speech, while still inhabited by a positive word of peace.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that they hear no futile speech except peace remains intact. The finding does not make every Garden description identical, claim that all speech is absent, or infer target-side morphology not supplied in the packet.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows provide exact target Arabic and explicit relation notes, but no target-side morphology or independent source-trust labels; the cross-text soundscape is therefore retained as a qualified synthesis.

findings.reader_payoff: Peace becomes perceptible both as what is heard and as the condition into which the Garden's residents have entered.
findings.containment: The focus still describes heard content. The finding does not turn سَلَامًا into a place-name, erase the speech function, or claim that every use of salām means achieved safety.

findings.title: Provision remains a settled allotment
findings.claim: The focus's لَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ participates in a wider Garden pattern where provision is repeatedly received, without depletion, and without measure, so the clause depicts settled provision rather than a one-time promise.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is رِزْقُهُمْ, possessed by the residents in the focus. The supplied Garden relations at 2:25 repeat provision as residents receive it, 38:54 calls the Garden reward provision with no exhaustion, and 40:40 describes believers receiving provision without measure. Their contact returns through the focus provision word and changes its temporal setting into continuing allotment.
findings.reader_payoff: Provision becomes something already assigned to the residents and reliably present, not merely a future item named in passing.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning of provision remains intact. The finding does not claim that provision is exclusively immaterial, abolish all distinction between residents, or import a complete Garden economy.

epistemic.reason: The cited connection rows give exact Garden Arabic and explicit provision relations, but target-side morphology and source-trust labels are absent; the continuing-allotment synthesis is therefore qualified.

findings.reader_payoff: Morning and evening function together as the visible edges of an ongoing daily rhythm for the residents' provision.
findings.containment: The literal morning and evening reading remains primary. No non-astronomical schedule, prescribed ritual, or target-side time morphology is inferred from the related cadence texts.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows explicitly note shared morning-evening markers but are retrieval nominations without target-side morphology or source-trust labels; the day-spanning cadence is retained as a qualified inference.

findings.title: Peace closes the exchange idle speech opens
findings.claim: The exception سَلَامًا meets wider scenes in which hearing futile or ignorant speech is followed by turning away and answering with peace, so the Garden's admitted utterance can be perceived as an active speech order that ends futile exchange.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are يَسْمَعُونَ, لَغْوًا, and سَلَامًا. At 28:55 the supplied text joins hearing laghw, turning from it, and saying salām; 25:63 answers ignorant speech with salām; 23:3 and 25:72 depict turning away from or passing by laghw. These contacts return through the focus hearing, excluded speech, and admitted peace and make the exception an enacted response pattern rather than only a label for quiet.
findings.reader_payoff: Peace becomes intelligible as the constructive response that completes the movement away from futile speech.
findings.containment: The focus still reports what the Garden residents hear. The finding does not claim that the Garden scene reproduces a worldly conversation, that every resident performs the same exchange, or that all speech is interactive.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows provide exact target Arabic and explicit ethical-response notes, but no target-side morphology or source-trust labels; the active-response synthesis is retained as qualified.

findings.title: Provision stands outside worldly comparison
findings.claim: Against a wider depiction of provision as a basis for worldly comparison, the focus states لَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ as direct belonging, allowing the Garden's provision to be perceived as an allotted good whose possession no longer needs a status contest.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier رِزْقُهُمْ is joined by the focus possession relation لَهُمْ. The supplied 16:71 text and connection note place provision in a worldly comparison of differentiated shares and equality within that comparison. Contact with the focus's direct possession statement produces a bounded contrast: provision is named as belonging to the residents without reproducing the comparative contest in the focus scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The provision clause acquires a social contour: its first emphasis is secure belonging, not a public ranking of who has more.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory contrast, not a claim that the Garden abolishes every distinction, proves equal quantities, or supplies a complete social theory. The focus's ordinary possession reading remains primary.

epistemic.reason: The single connection supplies exact Arabic and a stated worldly-comparison relation, but it is a weak retrieval nomination without target-side morphology or source-trust labeling; the noncompetitive contrast is consequently exploratory.
